claims.text: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation on this trip alone. The GPS trace measures 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km, or 115% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared — the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal — and the derived status is 'material' because the excess also exceeds 50%. The finding rests on the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement where the trace and the trip record disagree.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00109 and the same pickup event, and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: coverage is 100%, there are 207 fixes at a 10-second interval and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires. The excess may therefore be measured from the trace itself, and the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The additional-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 does not bite on this claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the threshold of 4, so this is not a claim that requires corroboration beyond the trace. The rider does not rely on any other field of either profile as a ground of decision, and POL-GEN-01 confines the profiles to credibility weighting.

The rider accepts that MSG-00109-001 asked the driver to stop at Jurong Point, and that the trace passes within about 38 m of that waypoint, so POL-RD-04 is engaged. But the clause exonerates a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to the instruction, and excludes only the excess 'between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. No artifact in this bundle measures that corridor-exit-and-rejoin distance, and the driver — who carries the burden of invoking the clause under POL-RD-08 — has identified none beyond the bare fact of the request. A five-minute errand does not of itself wipe out the whole 7.36 km of excess on the record as it stands.

No external traffic cause is available to the driver. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING: its admissibility status is MISSING, the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT fired, and its weight_multiplier is 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 a traffic-cause assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and with no advisory covering the trip window POL-RD-03 is unavailable as an exoneration. The excess is not reduced on any external-event ground.

On the measured excess the remedy is arithmetic, not discretionary. charged_total is 21.32. The recomputed optimal-route fare under POL-RD-02 is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 13.32, there being no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo line. The refund is 21.32 - 13.32 = 8.00, which the fare breakdown itself publishes as payable. That is 37.5% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the remedy is a partial refund of 8.00 rather than a full refund.

The rider does not press a full refund on pattern grounds, and says so rather than overreaching: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 511 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established and no uplift from the POL-RD-02 partial figure to FULL_REFUND is available. The POL-RD-02 partial figure is the ceiling the rider seeks.

claims.text: This was a rider-requested detour, not a driver frolic. MSG-00109-001 on the trip chat log was sent by the RIDER at 18:22:06 - one minute after the meter started at 18:21:10 - and it reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. That satisfies POL-RD-04(a), (b) and (c): the instruction is the rider's own, it is sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and it names a specific place the driver could act on.

POL-RD-04's corroboration limb is met on the pre-pass's own derived figures. The waypoint_hint attached to MSG-00109-001 resolves to VEN-JURONG-POINT at 1.339463, 103.706089, and the driver's GPS trace passes within 37.94 m of that waypoint - far inside the 200 m threshold POL-RD-04 sets - so the trace does corroborate the requested stop rather than contradict it.

Because the instruction is rider-sourced, timely, specific and corroborated, POL-RD-04 requires the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor to be excluded before POL-RD-01 is applied - and that out-and-back to Jurong Point is precisely the excess the rider now characterises as 'anyhow drive'. Assessed on the excess remaining after that exclusion, no driver-attributable deviation survives for the rider's refund claim to bite on, and POL-RD-02 has no non-exonerated excess to recompute against.

Separately, the fare breakdown shows the rider was billed for 9.6 km while the trace records 13.76 km - an unbilled shortfall of 4.16 km, well over the 1.0 km trigger. Under POL-RD-04 the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, that is SGD 3.15, within the SGD 15.00 cap. The driver's own counterparty statement says the same thing - he drove 13.8 km and the receipt shows 9.6 km - so the platform under-collected the distance he actually drove at the rider's request.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check does not bite here. The driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are 0 against 511 completed trips in the same window, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is met: there is no serial long-hauler on this artifact, no basis to resolve a balanced record against the driver, no basis to uplift a POL-RD-02 partial into a FULL_REFUND, and no basis for a conduct referral on this trip's account.

The rider has cleared her initial POL-RD-08 burden on a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so the burden shifts to the driver - and the driver discharges it by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause: the chat log EV-CHAT-00109 and POL-RD-04, corroborated by the 37.94 m waypoint approach on EV-GPS-00109. That is exactly what POL-RD-08 demands of the party invoking an exculpatory clause; a bare assertion that traffic was bad would not do, but a specific, trace-corroborated rider instruction does.

ruling.explanation: This is the Clementi-to-Bukit-Batok trip TRP-00109 of 21 July 2026. The rider was charged SGD 21.32. The platform's optimal-route fare is SGD 13.32, a difference of SGD 8.00, and the rider asked for that SGD 8.00 back. The GPS trace measures 13.76 km against an optimal 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km (EV-GPS-00109 / EV-TRIP-00109; POL-RD-01), which is a material deviation on its face. To the rider - why the SGD 8.00 is not refunded: the reason the trip ran long is your own request. At 18:22:06, about a minute after the meter started, you sent MSG-00109-001 in the in-app chat: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', with the Jurong Point PHV pickup point attached as the waypoint. The driver agreed (MSG-00109-002), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109) shows the vehicle passing within about 38 m of that exact waypoint - far inside the 200 m test in POL-RD-04. Jurong Point sits roughly 7 km west of the pickup, well outside the Clementi Road to Bukit Batok East Avenue 3 corridor, so the whole of the 7.36 km excess is the out-and-back you asked for. POL-RD-04 exonerates the driver for that distance; it is excluded before the POL-RD-01 threshold and POL-RD-02 are applied, no deviation remains, and the fare you paid stands. I have considered your argument that the clause exonerates only 'to the extent' the instruction is attributable and that no artifact measures the corridor-exit-and-rejoin distance. I reject it: the instruction named a point far off the optimal corridor and the unimpaired trace shows the vehicle going there and returning, so the measured excess is the detour and there is nothing left for POL-RD-02 to recompute against. To the driver - why you are paid: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00109) charged 9.60 km of distance while the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109) records 13.76 km. That is a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km trigger, and POL-RD-04 provides compensation at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12, rounded UP to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 cap. This matches your own statement that you drove 13.8 km while the receipt showed 9.6 km. Points that did not change the result: the rider is right that no traffic advisory is available - EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing - but the exoneration here rests on the rider's own instruction, not on any traffic cause, so that point does not revive the refund. The POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation check does not fire either way: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 511 completed trips in 90 days, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Figures used: charged_total 21.32; recomputed optimal-route fare 13.32; distance refund to the rider 0.00; driver compensation 3.15. The monetary effect of SGD 3.15 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this executes automatically.

To both parties, on trip TRP-00109 (Clementi MRT to Bukit Batok MRT).

What was driven. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00109 runs 13.76 km against the booked optimal of 6.4 km on EV-TRIP-00109 — an excess of 7.36 km, about 115% over. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%) and is a material deviation.

The rider's own instruction explains it. On the trip chat log EV-CHAT-00109 the rider wrote at 18:22:06, one minute after the meter started at 18:21:10: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', carrying the platform-resolved Jurong Point waypoint. The GPS trace passes within 37.94 m of that waypoint, inside the 200 m test, so the driver did what was asked. POL-RD-04 excludes the excess attributable to that requested detour before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and on this record the whole measured excess is that detour — the driven line is Clementi to Jurong Point to Bukit Batok, the itinerary the rider asked for, and nothing on the trace shows gratuitous driving beyond it. I have considered the rider's objection that no artifact puts a separate number on the corridor-exit-and-rejoin distance, but the continuous, unimpaired trace (207 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps) plus the requested waypoint leave no driver-attributable excess to refund. The rider's request for the optimal-route fare difference — 21.32 charged less 13.32 recomputed = 8.00 — is therefore refused.

Rider's remaining points. Her POL-RD-01 measurement and her POL-RD-08 burden-shifting point are accepted. Her POL-RD-13 point that no traffic advisory is on file is also correct, EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT), but the driver never asserted a traffic cause, so it decides nothing. Her POL-RD-06 point is accepted: the driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are 0 against 511 completed trips, so no pattern is established, the POL-RD-02 partial is not uplifted, and no conduct referral is made.

What the driver is owed. The fare breakdown EV-FARE-00109 bills the rider for 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km trigger. POL-RD-04 provides driver compensation at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 = SGD 3.15, within the SGD 15.00 cap. The driver is granted SGD 3.15, and amount_sgd carries the same figure as a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling requires. The rider's charge stands.

No ERP, toll or surcharge lines are present, so there is no billing-integrity referral. The monetary effect (SGD 3.15) does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00109 and the same pickup event, and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes: coverage is 100%, there are 207 fixes at a 10-second interval and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires. The excess may therefore be measured from the trace itself, and the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The additional-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 does not bite on this claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the threshold of 4, so this is not a claim that requires corroboration beyond the trace. The rider does not rely on any other field of either profile as a ground of decision, and POL-GEN-01 confines the profiles to credibility weighting.

The rider accepts that MSG-00109-001 asked the driver to stop at Jurong Point, and that the trace passes within about 38 m of that waypoint, so POL-RD-04 is engaged. But the clause exonerates a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to the instruction, and excludes only the excess 'between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. No artifact in this bundle measures that corridor-exit-and-rejoin distance, and the driver — who carries the burden of invoking the clause under POL-RD-08 — has identified none beyond the bare fact of the request. A five-minute errand does not of itself wipe out the whole 7.36 km of excess on the record as it stands.

No external traffic cause is available to the driver. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING: its admissibility status is MISSING, the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT fired, and its weight_multiplier is 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 a traffic-cause assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and with no advisory covering the trip window POL-RD-03 is unavailable as an exoneration. The excess is not reduced on any external-event ground.

On the measured excess the remedy is arithmetic, not discretionary. charged_total is 21.32. The recomputed optimal-route fare under POL-RD-02 is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 13.32, there being no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo line. The refund is 21.32 - 13.32 = 8.00, which the fare breakdown itself publishes as payable. That is 37.5% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the remedy is a partial refund of 8.00 rather than a full refund.

The rider does not press a full refund on pattern grounds, and says so rather than overreaching: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 511 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established and no uplift from the POL-RD-02 partial figure to FULL_REFUND is available. The POL-RD-02 partial figure is the ceiling the rider seeks.

This was a rider-requested detour, not a driver frolic. MSG-00109-001 on the trip chat log was sent by the RIDER at 18:22:06 - one minute after the meter started at 18:21:10 - and it reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. That satisfies POL-RD-04(a), (b) and (c): the instruction is the rider's own, it is sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and it names a specific place the driver could act on.

POL-RD-04's corroboration limb is met on the pre-pass's own derived figures. The waypoint_hint attached to MSG-00109-001 resolves to VEN-JURONG-POINT at 1.339463, 103.706089, and the driver's GPS trace passes within 37.94 m of that waypoint - far inside the 200 m threshold POL-RD-04 sets - so the trace does corroborate the requested stop rather than contradict it.

Because the instruction is rider-sourced, timely, specific and corroborated, POL-RD-04 requires the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor to be excluded before POL-RD-01 is applied - and that out-and-back to Jurong Point is precisely the excess the rider now characterises as 'anyhow drive'. Assessed on the excess remaining after that exclusion, no driver-attributable deviation survives for the rider's refund claim to bite on, and POL-RD-02 has no non-exonerated excess to recompute against.

Separately, the fare breakdown shows the rider was billed for 9.6 km while the trace records 13.76 km - an unbilled shortfall of 4.16 km, well over the 1.0 km trigger. Under POL-RD-04 the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, that is SGD 3.15, within the SGD 15.00 cap. The driver's own counterparty statement says the same thing - he drove 13.8 km and the receipt shows 9.6 km - so the platform under-collected the distance he actually drove at the rider's request.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check does not bite here. The driver's trailing-90-day deviation flags are 0 against 511 completed trips in the same window, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is met: there is no serial long-hauler on this artifact, no basis to resolve a balanced record against the driver, no basis to uplift a POL-RD-02 partial into a FULL_REFUND, and no basis for a conduct referral on this trip's account.

The rider has cleared her initial POL-RD-08 burden on a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so the burden shifts to the driver - and the driver discharges it by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause: the chat log EV-CHAT-00109 and POL-RD-04, corroborated by the 37.94 m waypoint approach on EV-GPS-00109. That is exactly what POL-RD-08 demands of the party invoking an exculpatory clause; a bare assertion that traffic was bad would not do, but a specific, trace-corroborated rider instruction does.
